name: TBL_ACCESS_RUN
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per CALL of SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT that ran (kept; a SKIPPED call deletes its own row, sql/1_setup.sql:837)

name: TBL_ACCESS_RUN.FINISHED_AT
summary: TIMESTAMP_LTZ: set at the end; readers pick the newest OK run by it

name: TBL_ACCESS_RUN.SOURCES
summary: VARIANT: dataset -> ACCOUNT_USAGE / SHOW / INFORMATION_SCHEMA / UNAVAILABLE

name: TBL_ACCESS_RUN.NOTES
summary: VARIANT: dataset -> why a fallback was used, roles skipped, error

name: TBL_ACCESS_GRANT
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per run x grantee role x privilege x granted_on x object x is_future (inferred, no constraint)

name: TBL_ACCESS_GRANT.GRANTEE_ROLE
summary: VARCHAR(255): account role, or database role as DB.ROLE

name: TBL_ACCESS_GRANT.GRANTED_ON
summary: VARCHAR(255): TABLE, VIEW, ROLE, DATABASE_ROLE, SCHEMA, ACCOUNT, ...

name: TBL_ACCESS_GRANT.OBJECT_NAME
summary: VARCHAR(2000): DB.SCHEMA.OBJECT unquoted; future grants DB.SCHEMA.<TABLE>; the granted role for role links

name: TBL_ACCESS_GRANT.IS_FUTURE
summary: BOOLEAN: TRUE for SHOW FUTURE GRANTS rows

name: TBL_ACCESS_GRANT.GRANTED_BY
summary: VARCHAR(255): role that granted it; NULL for future grants

name: TBL_ACCESS_USER_ROLE
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per run x user x granted role

name: TBL_ACCESS_USER_ROLE.ROLE_NAME
summary: VARCHAR(255): role granted to the user

name: TBL_ACCESS_USER
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per run x user

name: TBL_ACCESS_USER.TYPE
summary: VARCHAR(50): PERSON, SERVICE, LEGACY_SERVICE, empty = PERSON

name: TBL_ACCESS_USAGE
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per run x user x kind x name (GROUP BY at 1_setup.sql:321-329)

name: TBL_ACCESS_USAGE.QUERIES
summary: NUMBER: query count in the window (30 or 7 days)

name: TBL_ACCESS_TAG
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per run x object x domain x column x tag (inferred)

name: TBL_ACCESS_TAG.OBJECT_NAME
summary: VARCHAR(2000): DATABASE: DB, SCHEMA: DB.SCHEMA, TABLE/COLUMN: DB.SCHEMA.OBJECT

name: TBL_ACCESS_POLICY
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per run x policy x object x column, or per tag for tag-based policies (inferred)

name: TBL_ACCESS_POLICY.OBJECT_NAME
summary: VARCHAR(2000): DB.SCHEMA.OBJECT; empty for a policy set on a tag

name: TBL_ACCESS_POLICY.ARG_COLUMNS
summary: VARCHAR(2000): row access / conditional masking arguments

name: TBL_ACCESS_POLICY.POLICY_BODY
summary: VARCHAR: policy text; role checks read from it, not evaluated

name: TBL_ACCESS_STREAM
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per run x stream

name: TBL_ACCESS_OBJECT_USE
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per run x user x object x ISO week x action (GROUP BY at 1_setup.sql:491)

name: TBL_ACCESS_OBJECT_USE.OBJECT_NAME
summary: VARCHAR(2000): DB.SCHEMA.OBJECT as ACCESS_HISTORY names it

name: TBL_ACCESS_OBJECT_USE.WEEK
summary: DATE: Monday of the ISO week

name: TBL_ACCESS_FINDING
summary: Snowflake findings table; grain: one row per rule finding of the last SP_ACCESS_FINDINGS run (the call deletes every row first, sql/1_setup.sql:1133)

name: TBL_ACCESS_FINDING.RUN_ID
summary: VARCHAR(36): run the rules ran on

name: TBL_ACCESS_FINDING.GRANTEE
summary: VARCHAR(2000): user, role or object the finding is about

name: TBL_ACCESS_FINDING.KIND
summary: VARCHAR(20): user, admin, functional, technical, group, object

name: Access explorer data model
summary: Snapshot tables, in-memory dict and DuckDB copy

name: SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT(P_SOURCE)
summary: Owner's-rights Python procedure filling the 9 TBL_ACCESS_ data tables from ACCOUNT_USAGE or the SHOW fallback; run() skips if RUNNING. Every statement carries STATEMENT_TIMEOUT (TIMED, sql/1_setup.sql:212-217); SHOW / fallback statements run as async child jobs BATCH (16) at a time (many), heavy INSERTs at most WORKERS at once (later); ACCESS_HISTORY read once for object use + activity (history);

name: SP_ACCESS_FINDINGS(P_SETTINGS)
summary: Runs access.py rules on the last OK snapshot, writes TBL_ACCESS_FINDING

name: run
summary: Handler: RUNNING row first, async_ok probe (ASYNC), heavy steps started first (history), then grants, future, users, usage, tags, policies, streams; waits collected, row counts, keep only the last OK run

name: future
summary: Future grants via SHOW FUTURE GRANTS

name: object_use
summary: Object use step: copies the last OK run's weeks but its last two and reads ACCESS_HISTORY from that Monday on (use_sql(since)); plan=True returns (since, sql) for history(); skipped / not readable -> SKIPPED / UNAVAILABLE, the run stays OK

name: data_objects
summary: Tables/views of this run's grants, for per-object fallbacks

name: TF_ACCESS_OF
summary: Worksheet table function over the last OK run (sql/1_setup.sql:920-979)

name: TF_WHO_CAN
summary: Worksheet table function over the last OK run: HELD = the grants on the object, then one walk up per holder role, not per privilege (sql/1_setup.sql:1004-1025)

name: TF_CAN
summary: Worksheet table function over the last OK run: the TF_ACCESS_OF walk with the object and privilege filter in the grant join (OWNERSHIP counts, VIA_OWNERSHIP), not after it (sql/1_setup.sql:1028-1075)

name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE
summary: Snowflake account usage views (lag up to ~2 h, README.html:717)

summary: ACCOUNT_USAGE view read by the snapshot (sql/1_setup.sql:379)

summary: ACCOUNT_USAGE view read by the snapshot (sql/1_setup.sql:381)

summary: ACCOUNT_USAGE view read by the snapshot (sql/1_setup.sql:498)

name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.TAG_REFERENCES
summary: ACCOUNT_USAGE view read by the snapshot (sql/1_setup.sql:546)

name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.POLICY_REFERENCES
summary: ACCOUNT_USAGE view read by the snapshot (sql/1_setup.sql:598)

name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.MASKING_POLICIES
summary: ACCOUNT_USAGE view read by the snapshot (sql/1_setup.sql:599)

name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ROW_ACCESS_POLICIES
summary: ACCOUNT_USAGE view read by the snapshot (sql/1_setup.sql:600)

name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ACCESS_HISTORY
summary: ACCOUNT_USAGE view read by the snapshot (sql/1_setup.sql:658)

name: snapshot
summary: The last OK run of the snapshot tables, WORKERS tables at a time via each() (SELECT * EXCLUDE (RUN_ID), access.py:494-499); old = the data held (cache.last): the same RUN_ID in the shape this code reads -> returned after one small query (access.py:487-492); a run that finishes mid-read restarts the read on it; ACTIVITY=0: OBJECT_USE / ACTIVITY not read, sources SKIPPED (access.py:508-511); ACTIVIT

name: live
summary: SOURCE=direct: the whole account read now with the caller's role, same dict as snapshot(). Two waves: every ACCOUNT_USAGE probe at once (access.py:820-826), then every readable view WORKERS at a time (access.py:895); SHOW fallbacks as SHOW_THREADS waves, SHOW DATABASES once; object use and activity from one ACCESS_HISTORY read (history_sql, access.py:891-904), only the weeks / days old_use / old l

name: mine
summary: My access: the logged-in user's own access, live, with their own rights; one each() wave of the role SHOWs, SHOW GRANTS TO USER, DESC USER and the 30-day QUERY_HISTORY usage (access.py:669-676). Writes nothing; no OBJECT_USE key.

name: fake
summary: Fake data set, same dict shape

name: fake_previous
summary: Fake previous snapshot for What changed

name: only
summary: Demo of mine(): one user's slice of a data set

name: build
summary: Fills module lookups from the snapshot dict

name: use_sql
summary: use_sql(since): object use from ACCESS_HISTORY from a Monday on (use_start), ACCESS_HISTORY scanned once (CTE A), per user, object, ISO week and READ / WRITE; the same text in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT (sql/1_setup.sql:652-668)

name: snapshot dict
summary: dict(run, GRANT, USER_ROLE, USER, USAGE, TAG, POLICY, STREAM, OBJECT_USE, ACTIVITY): one list of row dicts per TBL_ACCESS_ table (no RUN_ID column); OBJECT_USE / ACTIVITY None when the table is missing (OPTIONAL), [] with sources SKIPPED under ACTIVITY=0

name: TABLES / OPTIONAL
summary: Tables snapshot() reads; OBJECT_USE and ACTIVITY optional

name: read_shared
summary: fake() / with_query(live with the ACTIVITY and OBJECT_USE rows of cache.last) / with_query(snapshot with old=cache.last: the same run costs one small query) by MODE and SOURCE

name: reload
summary: POST /api/reload (run in a thread pool, so /api/progress answers meanwhile): rebuild = CALL SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT('AUTO') under tracked(), load, page; drops the cache

name: get
summary: (data, fetched_at): from memory, else the local file, else fn() (stored in both); a read runs under its key's own lock (lock(key)), so another key never waits.

name: keep_prev
summary: turns the replaced .pkl into <key>.prev.pkl unless same run

name: drop
summary: Read again next time: out of memory under the key's lock (the memory copy kept in OLD, so last() still finds it inside Snowflake), and the local file set aside.

name: name
summary: cache key: account, source, location, user, role

name: sql_copy
summary: Write data set d to .cache/access.duckdb, schema schema(key): this read as the TBL_ACCESS_ tables, the read before as _PREV; one bulk INSERT per table (text lists UNNESTed side by side, TRY_CAST per column, cache.py:266-271) under SQL_LOCK (one writer for every key).

name: sql_wanted
summary: whether a read gets a SQL copy

name: schema
summary: DuckDB schema of a cache key

name: COLUMNS
summary: DuckDB column lists of the 9 TBL_ACCESS_ tables (no FINDING)

name: CACHE_HOURS
summary: hours a .pkl is kept (24; 0 = memory only)

name: .cache/<key>.pkl
summary: pickled snapshot dict per cache key

name: TBL_ACCESS_ACTIVITY
summary: Snowflake snapshot table; grain: one row per run x UTC day x user x role x client x object x action x query type x app (final GROUP BY of activity_sql, sql/1_setup.sql:741); HOURS = queries per UTC hour; 60 days kept, copied forward from the last OK run

name: TBL_ACCESS_ACTIVITY.DAY
summary: DATE: UTC day of the query start (CONVERT_TIMEZONE('UTC', QUERY_START_TIME))

name: TBL_ACCESS_ACTIVITY.CLIENT
summary: VARCHAR(255): SESSIONS.CLIENT_APPLICATION_ID without its version; NULL when SESSIONS is not readable

name: TBL_ACCESS_ACTIVITY.OBJECT_NAME
summary: VARCHAR(2000): DB.SCHEMA.OBJECT as ACCESS_HISTORY names it

name: activity_sql (SP)
summary: SP copy of access.activity_sql (same text, test_sql.test_activity): ACCESS_HISTORY (since day) x QUERY_HISTORY (role, statement, APP from QUERY_TAG; the app's QUERY_TAG and STREAMLIT_APP left out, filled from !define at deploy, sql/1_setup.sql:210-211) x SESSIONS (client), per UTC day..statement and app, HOURS = OBJECT_AGG(UTC hour, queries)

name: activity (SP step)
summary: SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT step: copies the last OK run rows older than since (all columns, HOURS and APP included), inserts activity_sql(since); plan=True returns the plan for history(); skipped -> SKIPPED, not readable -> UNAVAILABLE, the run stays OK; an error deletes this run's ACTIVITY rows

name: ACCOUNT_USAGE.SESSIONS
summary: Session -> client application id; optional (no client when not readable)

name: TBL_ACCESS_ACTIVITY_PREV (DuckDB)
summary: DuckDB copy of the read before

name: fallback (SP)
summary: SP helper: None = read ACCOUNT_USAGE.<view>; else the reason to fall back (SHOW forced, or the view not readable); P_SOURCE=ACCOUNT_USAGE raises instead

name: TBL_ACCESS_ACTIVITY.HOURS
summary: VARIANT: {UTC hour of day: queries} (OBJECT_AGG in activity_sql); added to older tables by TABLE_ACTIVITY_HOURS (may fail)

name: TBL_ACCESS_ACTIVITY.APP
summary: VARCHAR(2000): the Streamlit app the queries ran for (QUERY_TAG StreamlitName / streamlitName), else NULL; added by TABLE_ACTIVITY_APP (may fail)

name: async_ok (SP)
summary: One SHOW ROLES LIMIT 1 as an async child job (collect_nowait); a failure turns the async path off for the run (ASYNC)

name: many (SP)
summary: rows() of each statement, BATCH (16) at a time as async child jobs, in order; a failed one gives its exception; one that cannot start async runs with collect()

name: later (SP)
summary: Starts a heavy INSERT ... SELECT as an async child job, at most WORKERS at once (PENDING); its wait() gives the step's (source, note): ok, or UNAVAILABLE with this run's rows deleted

name: history (SP step)
summary: Object use + activity from one ACCESS_HISTORY scan: each step copies its earlier rows, then one INSERT ALL of history_sql fills both tables; on failure each step reads alone (not after a timeout, or once the run failed)
